title: Secant Slope on the Parabola y = x^2
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Two distinct points (a, a^2) and (b, b^2) lie on the parabola y = x^2. Show that the slope of the secant line through them equals a + b, and interpret what happens as b approaches a.

steps.title: Set Up the Slope Quotient
steps.explanation: Slope is change in output over change in input; both points lie on y = x^2 so their heights are a^2 and b^2.
steps.why: Distinctness a != b keeps the denominator nonzero, which is required before any cancellation.

steps.title: Factor the Difference of Squares
steps.explanation: The numerator is the classic difference-of-squares pattern and splits into the product of the sum and the very factor appearing in the denominator.
steps.why: Factoring exposes the common factor (a - b) so the quotient can be reduced.

steps.title: Cancel and Conclude
steps.explanation: Removing the shared nonzero factor leaves the strikingly simple result that the secant slope is just the sum of the two x-coordinates.
steps.why: Cancellation of a nonzero factor is a legitimate equivalence; the simplified expression still equals the original quotient for all a != b.

steps.title: Pass to the Tangent Limit
steps.explanation: Letting the second point slide toward the first turns the secant into the tangent, and the slope a + b becomes 2a, the derivative of x^2 at a.
steps.why: The secant-slope formula is the difference quotient in disguise; its limit as the points merge defines the tangent slope.
